newsitem.title: JAPAN: Some Japan regional bank stock down on Tokuyo fall.
newsitem.headline: Some Japan regional bank stock down on Tokuyo fall.

text.p: Shares in some regional banks were depressed on Tuesday afternoon by the sharp fall in Tokuyo City Bank Ltd's shares, brokers said.
As of 0458 GMT, Bank of Kansai Ltd shares were down 45 yen at 595 yen on the Osaka bourse. Hanshin Bank Ltd was down 64 yen at 329 yen.
"Ever since the Finance Ministry suspended some of Hanwa Bank Ltd's business operations, investors have become sensitive about regional banks," a second-tier broker said.

Last week, the Ministry of Finance announced that it halted operations at Hanwa, a regional bank, except for withdrawals of deposits, because the bank could not recover its bad loans and was unable to operate as a going concern.
Brokers said that as in the case with Tokuyo City Bank, selling linked with the expiry of six-month margin transactions was doing its part in bringing down the regional banks' share prices.

"Some investors engage in margin trade of such bank shares to obtain fast profits," one broker said. "When the deadline approaches, they tend to sell off what they have, which in turn invites more selling, leading to a tumble in share prices."
